Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.
Suggested line: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back up the path to the glowing arch.
Why: Folds in the earlier note: names the landmark the player can actually see.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops.
Suggested line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops. Everyone complained. Everything worked.
Why: A list becomes a Maren line with a sting, and seeds 'they argued and needed each other anyway'.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.
Suggested line: Still here, dearie? {villain} would love you to sit by my fire forever. Don't give him the satisfaction. Give me back my chair.
Why: The current 'some roads would walk themselves' turn doesn't land; this keeps the push out the door and ends on her sting.

Speaker: Sable
Effective line: You start with plain neutral cards. The Paths are where the power is. Browse, buy, then put it all to work at the Deck Station.
Suggested line: You start with plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable, dull. The Paths are where the power is. Buy some, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
Why: The tutorial line could be anyone's; 'darling' and a three-beat pitch make it Sable's.

Speaker: Tilly Tonic
Effective line: Potions and charms, back for more! Equip them on your Character screen for fights - maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
Suggested line: Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
Why: 'Potions and charms, back for more!' reads as if the potions came back; same info, cleaner.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Whatever it is, it is not open for business.
Suggested line: Whatever it is, it sounds like it has been on hold for a very long time.
Why: 'Not open for business' is used three times in town; this one sets up the ghosts' customer-service voice instead.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: Whatever is down there is not open for business. Yet.
Suggested line: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.
Why: Second 'not open for business'; this hints at Bellows before you meet him and keeps the 'not yet'.

Speaker: Auntie Alembic
Effective line: Whenever you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, the extras turn into essence of that card's Path.
Suggested line: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.
Why: Same rule, in Alembic's soft voice instead of a tooltip's.

Speaker: Pip Threadwell
Effective line: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone has to defeat the person who owns it first.
Suggested line: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.
Why: Gives Pip's teaser his melodrama and a punchline instead of trailing off.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a hand on every card. Bring your best deck.
Suggested line: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a fist for each. Bring your best deck.
Why: 'A hand on every card' is unclear; a fist per Path sets up the Fourth Fist event.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: Another win for the books. The crowd roars (and tosses you some coins).
Suggested line: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Some coins for you. From the crowd. The crowd is me.
Why: Puts the replay win in Bellows' loud-then-small voice; the coins stay.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: The puzzle got the better of you. Study the board and try again.
Suggested line: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Study the board. Try again. It's not going anywhere.
Why: The only Bellows line with no Bellows in it; keeps the advice.

Speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
Effective line: Walk into a town, and its station wakes up. Then you can rip between any two of them. Thank you for ripping with the Express.
Suggested line: After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.
Why: The first half repeated the box before it; cut the repeat and give the sign-off a joke.

Speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
Effective line: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest where you all started out?
Suggested line: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?
Why: 'Where you all started out' reads oddly; this matches the station blurb.

Speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
Effective line: I will be here, guarding the drawer.
Suggested line: I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.
Why: A bare closing line gets one deadpan Bertram turn.

Speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
Effective line: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol One.
Suggested line: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol Three.
Why: Protocol One is already 'assess the customer's gait'; Three is unused.

Speaker: Auntie Alembic
Effective line: The flasks are humming today, dear. Don't touch the red one. It bites.
Suggested line: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.
Why: Seeds the four-colours clue as a vendor noticing it without knowing why; the red flask joke lives on elsewhere.

Speaker: Brick Bronson (corrupted)
Effective line: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Never broke, they say. Huh.
Suggested line: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.
Why: 'Never broke, they say' is hard to parse; this keeps the crack in Brick and points at Flex.

Speaker: Crosspath townsfolk
Effective line: Lovely day for a quest, isn't it? Shh. Not too lovely. Somebody's listening.
Suggested line: Say what you like about His Perfection, the wells are clean. Shh. Don't, actually.
Why: Swaps a generic 'lovely day for a quest' for Primm's real reform and the watched town in one bark.
